description_long.current:
On July 14, 2019, Donald Trump tweeted that four progressive Democratic congresswomen—Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Ilhan Omar, Ayanna Pressley, and Rashida Tlaib, collectively known as “The Squad”—should “go back” to the “totally broken and crime infested places from which they came.” All four were U.S. citizens; three were born in the United States. The phrasing invoked a long-standing racist trope that treats people of color as foreign regardless of citizenship or birthplace.

The remarks drew condemnation from civil rights leaders, international figures, former presidents, and others. The House of Representatives formally voted to condemn Trump’s comments as racist; only four Republicans joined Democrats in support of the resolution. The episode put a sitting president’s public language at the center of a national debate over racism, belonging, and political attacks on elected officials.

The House vote recorded congressional condemnation, but it did not undo the comments or impose a legal penalty. The supplied account characterizes the remarks as among the most overtly racist public statements by a sitting American president in modern history. Reuters reported the tweets and noted that all four lawmakers were U.S. citizens, with three born in the United States. The immediate consequence was widespread public and political censure; the record does not establish further formal consequences for Trump arising from the episode.
